text: Using a two-phase curriculum that trains first on confident weak-labeled examples and then on the full weak-labeled set with the learning rate scaled by 0.1 in phase two, we supervised a qwen2.5-7b strong student with gpt2-large weak labels across 5 seeds. The weak supervisor reaches 0.58 accuracy and the strong ceiling is 0.82, while the curriculum-trained student attains transfer accuracy of 0.77 with a standard error of 0.03. This corresponds to a performance gap recovered of 0.8 with a standard error of 0.12, against a baseline PGR of 0.18; the margin exceeds two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so the curriculum shows a reliable improvement over the baseline on this setup. Caveats worth noting: the baseline PGR is reported without an accompanying standard error, the evaluation covers a single weak–strong model pair, and 5 seeds with a PGR standard error of 0.12 leaves the effect size itself loosely pinned down.
